agad-338-446.summary: Branicki tells Potocki that the plan agreed at Warsaw meets obstacles but must not be lost from sight, that the most pressing matter is the abuse an envoy (probably the stolnik of Lithuania) makes of his mission, and proposes a manifesto to be published together with Potocki's house and other patriots, to meet at the end of the next month.
agad-338-446.en:
From reading446.md, with the same holes. [480] is an unread code group, [?word] is a doubtful reading, and a word in square brackets is supplied.

Białystok, 22 March 1757.

Monseigneur,

I have received the letter that Your Excellency did me the honour of writing to me on the 6th of this month, and I do not lose a moment in replying.

Although the plan agreed at Warsaw meets obstacles from our friends, I do not at all believe that we should lose sight of it.

I even foresee events that will make carrying it out indispensable.

But the most pressing matter that must occupy us at this moment is the abuse that Mr the [?Stolnik] of Lithuania is making of his mission.

agad-338-1398.summary: A field report from the Russian army under Apraxin at the frontier of Prussia: famine and requisitions in Lithuania, deputies of the Prussian towns come to submit, an army of sixty thousand, rumours of poison in the flour.
agad-338-1398.en:
This follows the French reading, with the same holes. [795] is an unread code group, [?word] is a doubtful reading, and a letter in square brackets is supplied.

From each place I have the honour to send you my deep respects [795]. And I believe my letters written from Vilna have reached your hands. [775]

I am now with Mr Siruc, Castellan of Witebsk, my father-in-law, six leagues beyond Kowno.

The news from this place is that Count Apraxin is still at his headquarters at [?Ludwinow], seven leagues from the frontier of Prussia, and it is believed he will not enter Prussia so quickly.

The shortage here is extraordinary, especially of f[l]our, and even all the pastures around where the army passed, for three leagues, are completely ruined by a great number of horses.

agad-338-1399.summary: An insider reports on the party of the Lithuanian grand hetman: a congress at Iwie agrees to deposit 146,000 francs at Koydanow to buy the coming dietines and the Tribunal of 1757, five lords' shares are listed (they add up), and the writer proposes a direct correspondence with the French minister.
agad-338-1399.en:
From reading.md, with the same holes. [195] is an unread code group, and [?word] is a doubtful reading. Clear passages and cipher passages run on together here. The transcription marks which is which.

Sir,

I have received yours of the 6th of this month. I would very gladly have answered at once, if time had allowed it in any way, but I was still travelling when the post went out, and we were hardly left the time required, so I could not do as I wished.

I have however made up for this by having my master do what I would have done myself, if time had allowed: I got him to send you a copy of the letter from Mr [195], dated the 30th of last month, which was not answered by this post. When it is, I will not fail to have a copy sent to you.

agad-338-1400.summary: A bloody dietine at Brest, with massacred gentlemen and brother against brother; the rival party has spent 200,000 francs in the palatinates and elected its own deputies; the palatine decides not to risk the party's own money; signed Boeven.
agad-338-1400.en:
From reading.md, with the same holes. [385] is an unread code group, and [?word] is a doubtful reading.

Nieśwież, 11 September 1756

Sir,

Every day we hear here very tragic news of the dietines of our Lithuania. Whichever way one turns, one meets only the corpses of gentlemen massacred at these riotous assemblies, which are carried to the courts and to the Tribunal to be presented there: the deadly result of this hatred that is tearing apart the Republic.

This time at Brest of Lithuania, for electing the deputies to the general Diet, there was a dietine of the most riotous kind. Everything there breathed only rage, fury and carnage. Brother against brother, kin against kin, were let loose with the utmost inhumanity.

Count Sapieha, the Palatine, was there to keep good order, and to try to bring about a peaceful choice of deputies in this palatinate who could serve our aims.
